Mubi Takes Worldwide To Eleanor Coppola’s Documentary ‘Making Marie Antoinette’
Mubi Take Worldwide Rights on ‘Making Marie Antoinette’

piece.headline: Mubi Buys Making Marie Antoinette; the Archive Tracks the Film From Cannes Boos to Canon
piece.dek: Eleanor Coppola's set footage becomes a feature documentary just as the 2006 film's reception record completes its arc.
piece.summary: Mubi has taken worldwide rights to Making Marie Antoinette, built from Eleanor Coppola's on-set footage. The archive's record for the 2006 film shows an early Oscar, a late canon entry, and a reception file that moved in between.
piece.facts_html:
Confirmed: Mubi has taken worldwide rights to Eleanor Coppola's documentary Making Marie Antoinette, per Deadline and IndieWire. The film is assembled from roughly 80 hours of previously unseen set footage shot by Eleanor Coppola at Versailles, timed to the production's 20th anniversary.

Reported, per coverage of the announcement: the cut was edited by Aaron Matthews and narrated by Diane Lane, voicing journal entries Eleanor Coppola wrote during the 2005 shoot. No release date is set; Mubi says plans will follow. The precedent is direct: Eleanor Coppola previously turned behind-the-scenes footage from Apocalypse Now into Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker's Apocalypse in 1991.

The subject's history is on file. Marie Antoinette premiered at Cannes in 2006, where it competed for the Palme d'Or. It drew both applause and boos at press screenings; Roger Ebert noted that only a couple of journalists booed and that the media sensationalized the event, per Wikipedia's account of the coverage.
piece.reading_html:
The archive's record for the film is short and its shape is specific. The honors table holds one row: the Best Costume Design win at the 79th Academy Awards, logged here as 2007. The canon table also holds one row: the BBC's 100 Greatest Films Directed by Women, 2019 edition, at #63. Twelve years separate the two entries.

The reception file spans that gap: a New York Times verdict from the premiere year, a Vulture entry from 2013, and RogerEbert.com's reading that Coppola brilliantly sidesteps a beheading. The TakeScore sits at 17, split 16 prestige to 4 discovery. The scorecard describes a film whose standing runs through awards and lists rather than through rediscovery traffic.

The rehabilitation is attributed, not asserted. Coppola herself told Vanity Fair the film "was a flop" and that its afterlife has been satisfying, per IndieWire. Far Out wrote this year that it has become an undisputed classic, and Mental Floss files it among Cannes-booed films now considered among Coppola's finest work. The new documentary revisits the production those verdicts were reacting to.
piece.bottom_html: A one-row honors table in 2007, a one-row canon table in 2019, and a reception file that moved in between: that is the record Making Marie Antoinette now reopens, this time from the mother's side of the camera. See the full scorecard at the film's TakeScore page.
piece.deposit: Marie Antoinette (2006): a twelve-year gap in the record between its only honors entry (2007 Costume Design Oscar) and its first tracked canon appearance (BBC 2019, #63).
